title: Rejection never renders when the snap target is node id 0 (the residential node) — the drag_to sentinel collides with a live id, so AC1's terminal-to-terminal example draws nothing
detail: topology_make zeroes next_node_id; seed_fixture spawns residential first, so residential is node id 0. Dragging content_host to residential sets drag_to=0 (the 'none' sentinel) while valid=.Terminal_To_Terminal. The gate suppresses the rejection entirely.
recommended_fix: Distinguish 'no snap' from 'snapped to id 0' (e.g. drag_snapped bool or ids starting at 1), and draw the rejection whenever valid != .None during an active drag.

title: Cursor-anchored rejection clips past WIN_W near the map's right edge — long labels exceed the remaining window width where the short cost label fits
evidence:
WIN_W :: 1280

			draw_text(app, reject_label(app.drag.valid), i32(cur.x)+12, i32(cur.y)-14, 16, rl.Color{200, 60, 60, 255})

	case .Terminal_To_Terminal: return "terminals connect via routers only"

	case .Router_Ports_Full: return "router ports full - demolish a pipe or upgrade"

	rl.DrawText(cstring(raw_data(cbuf)), x, y, size, col)
detail: No clamp before draw_text. With w_tiles=40/tile_px=26 the rightmost node sits at screen x=1096 and the snap radius lets the cursor reach ~1129, leaving ~139px to WIN_W. The 33-46 char labels (~300-400px at 16px) truncate; "cost N" fits.
recommended_fix: Clamp the draw position into [0, WIN_W - text_width] (or flip the label left of the cursor near the right edge) before draw_text.
